title.narrative: TROCAIRE- Fred genom jämställdhet och motståndskraftiga samhällen i Ituri
TROCAIRE- Peace through gender equitable and resilient communities in Ituri

description.narrative: Given the Ituri context of instability trough displacement, lack of women’s empowerment, SGBV and gender inequality, the project proposes to address issues of women’s participation in informal and formal decision-making. These processes include those where conflict dynamics are influenced and discussed and around protection from SGBV and equitable access to land. To create an enabling environment for this to take place in Mambasa and Djugu, Trócaire aims to empower women economically, so that they can have the time and space to engage more meaningfully in the social empowerment work and protection from SGBV that the project will be supporting. Trócaire’s empowerment approach aims at strengthening individual and community capacities to engage with duty bearers and to influence plans and policies that directly affect their lives. A conflict sensitive approach will be applied throughout the project so that Trócaire activities and partners will be enabled to promote peace and contribute to reduced levels of destructive and violent conflict in target zones. The overall goal of the project is to contribute to peaceful and gender equitable communities in Mambasa and Djugu Territories, Ituri Province, DRC. 3 long term outcomes have been identified which the project will aim to reach: Women, particularly young women are socially and economically empowered to participate in both conflict and peace-related formal and informal decision-making processes at all levels;Women, girls and boys are free from violence and its associated risks ;Civil Society Organisations working on gender equality and women’s rights are strengthened and deliver on their objectives. A total of 16,000 people (11,200 women and 4,800 men) are being targeted by the proposed project. This figure is calculated based on 4,000 households benefiting from the proposed interventions within Djugu and Mambasa Territories. This program will cover 27 villages including 13 in Djugu and 14 Mambasa. These villages have already been supported by Trócaire in humanitarian and livelihood, and this intervention will continue to build on and consolidate its work. In Mambasa, Trócaire has been working with IDPs and host communities in Mambasa territory through food, NFI and WASH interventions while in Djugu, it has worked since 2010 targeting vulnerable women in a context of recurrent ethnic conflicts and limited accessibility.

Det föreslagna projektet från Trocaire kommer att lyfta frågor om kvinnors deltagande i formella likväl informella beslutsfattande processer. Detta inkluderar processer där konflikt är en faktor samt kring frågor som rör skydd från könsbaserat våld och jämställd tillgång till land. För att skapa en miljö där detta ska kunna ske avser Trocaire att stödja kvinnor ekonomiskt. Syftet med ett ekonomiskt stöd är att kvinnor ska kunna frigöra tid och möjlighet att engagera sig mer i det sociala arbetet för att stärka kvinnans roll och minska dess utsatthet för könsbaserat våld.
Trociares mål om ökat kvinnligt deltagande syftar till att stärka individers och gruppers förmåga att engagera sig och att påverka planer och policys som har direkt inverkan på deras liv.
Ett konfliktmedvetet tillvägagångssätt kommer att tillämpas för projektet så att Trocaires aktiviteter och dess partners kan främja fred och bidra till ett samhälle med mindre våld och konflikter.
Det övergripande målet för projektet är att bidra till fredliga och jämställda samhällen i områdena Mambasa och Djugu i Ituri-provinsen i DRK. Tre långsiktiga resultat har identifierats som projektet har som mål att uppnå:
1. Kvinnor, särskilt unga kvinnor, är socialt och ekonomiskt stärkta för att delta i konflikt- och fredsrelaterade beslutsprocesser på alla nivåer; 2. Kvinnor, flickor och pojkar är fria ifrån våld och våldsrelaterade risker; 3. Civilsamhällsorganisationer arbetar med jämställdhetsfrågor och kvinnors rättigheter stärks enligt uppsatta mål.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
The third year of this project faced many challenges in its implementation. The President of the Republic has declared a state of siege in the province of Ituri. All planned advocacy activities with the Provincial Assembly and Provincial Government have been suspended until further notice. It should be noted that the civil administration was changed with the military administration. By mentioning also the COVID-19 with many restrictions before being released. This had an impact on the implementation and the politico-socio-economic life of the communities living in this area.
It should be noticed :
The rate of implementation of field activities in year 3 as of July 2021 is as follows :
90% of the level of implementation of activities within the two territories covered by the project by 7 implementing partners 63% of the level of implementation of activities by Trocaire to date, as some consultancies are in progress, taking into account the procedures to be followed.
To date, 4397 beneficiaries have been reached (i.e. 68%), including 2637 women and 1760 men, out of 6426 expected beneficiaries, including 4326 women and 2100 men for the entire project.
Speaking of the Sustainable Livelihoods component, notably income and land:
14 fish ponds, including 7 in Djugu and 7 in Mambasa, were developed for 431 beneficiaries, 299 in Mambasa and 131 in Djugu, 14 mixed mills, 14 sheds, 14 small warehouses for storing agricultural products,
90 small machines for groundnut paste and 15 machines for cassava leaves (sombé) have been distributed to the 14 communities, 7 of which are in Djugu and 7 in Mambasa, and all of them are operational and self-managed 13,132 kg of seeds were distributed (7892 kg in Djugu and 5240 kg in Mambasa).
Among which 4808 kg of yellow maize, 7274 kg of beans and 1050 kg of soya beans will be distributed to 622 direct beneficiaries in Djugu.
7 lowlands and 10 water retention basins developed for the production of vegetable crops (cabbage, aubergine, amaranth, onions, etc.) all year round in the two territories, including (3 lowlands, 5 water retention basins in Mambasa and 5 lowlands through irrigation channels and 5 water retention basins in Djugu.
1,200 beneficiaries, including 801 women and 399 men, were given technical support in the production of food crops and vegetables in their individual and community fields.
54 MUSO (Mutuelles de Solidarité) set up in 27 villages of Djugu and Mambasa have been supported in the transparent management of the funds made available to them and the use of management tools.
931 beneficiaries, including 514 women and 417 men, are involved in the IGAs developed, namely: small-scale trade in consumer and manufactured goods, sale of telephone units and credits, opening of a restaurant, etc.
Veterinary support and monitoring has been provided to the 1787 goat breeders distributed to 1200 beneficiaries during the 3 years of project implementation 32 community dialogues on equitable access to land in which 1013 people participated, including 685 women and 328 men.
16 training sessions, including 4 in Djugu and 4 in Mambasa, on the concepts of land rights and other laws that protect women's rights for leaders; men and women were organised for 640 people, including 406 men and 234 women.
3 community radio stations broadcast programmes on women's access to and control of land.
33 community awareness sessions on education, equitable decision-making and division of labour within the household between women and their male partners 670 Land rights extension tools produced in local language in collaboration with the Ituri land cell distributed in Mambasa and Djugu.
556 Women and 53 Men participate in awareness-raising literacy sessions in Djudu and Mambasa centres Facilitation of the updating and development of operational plans for 4 LDPs of 4 ETDs in Mambasa and the development of 7 PDCs in Djugu.
Facilitation of the establishment of two CSO consultation frameworks as well as accountability structures in 4 chiefdoms and 11 groups.
4 social action analyses to prioritise discriminatory social norms with 85 people (40 women and 45 men) representing 4 communities 291 people (200 men and 91 women) participated in training sessions on positive masculinity.
2 synergies of women's organisations formed for the defence of women's rights and which accompany women leaders and aspirants.And do advocacy in network with the CPCs. A provincial advocacy mechanism (CLPP) set up to analyse the advocacy needs of community structures.
13 community protection structures set up in Mambasa territory, each composed of 15 members, 8 of whom are women and 7 men. 22 PSAs trained in case management.
12 and 10 women 13 early warning committees on protection and SGBV installed in 13 villages of Mambasa for family awareness and mediation.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
